description: Planted falsifiers. SPEC 18: at least one defect per proof family, and the corresponding checker must fail.

falsifiers.plants: formalProof level without a Lean declaration
citing the Atlas seal's cover check as universal coverage
falsifiers.expectedRejector: AT-001 scope-blindness lemma plus AT-002 absence check
falsifiers.note: Fails if Atlas.seal_implies_universal_coverage is supplied without a real proof, or if the blindness lemma that makes its absence principled is removed.

falsifiers.plants: a stale .olean masking a root module that does not elaborate
falsifiers.note: Regression guard. This defect really occurred: lakefile used globs .submodules, which never builds the root, so `lake build` reported green while two modules declared clashing Fault types.

falsifiers.expectedRejector: xtask sources firewall, SPEC 10.1 dependency firewall
falsifiers.note: Guards the property that makes GlobalOptimal meaningful: the competitor universe must be defined without reference to the artifact it will be compared against. Otherwise the theorem is a statement about a universe built around its own answer.

falsifiers.plants: a manifest stage containing its own identity, or a backward reference between stages
falsifiers.note: SPEC 4 requires the identity stages be acyclic: no manifest contains its own identity and no two stages hash each other. A cyclic manifest could be made to attest to itself.

falsifiers.plants: a weakened GlobalOptimal whose competitor quantifier is restricted by a scope predicate
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the Iff.rfl schema binding in WasmGemmGnaf/Conformance/Schema.lean
falsifiers.note: SPEC 1 requires the gate to compare the compiled UNFOLDED definition against the frozen WGG-GO-1 schema, and says a theorem scoped to a subset of the competitor universe SHALL have a different name. Iff.rfl is what makes that comparison definitional. The falsifier elaborates GlobalOptimalOver <scope> against the same frozen schema and requires it to FAIL, with the unweakened binding as a control so it cannot pass by failing for an unrelated reason.

falsifiers.plants: a required declaration that is present, correctly named, and choice-tainted
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the SPEC 15 inventory, which reports TAINTED and does not count it as discharged
falsifiers.note: SPEC 4: Classical.choice SHALL NOT produce executable witnesses. A Fintype instance, an enumerator and a decision procedure are DATA, so a choice-tainted closure disqualifies them however well-named they are. An external audit found a name-only check crediting exactly this shape. The planted witness is elaborated against the real compiled environment, so the axiom closure driving the verdict is Lean's own answer; a choice-free witness under the same name is the control and must still be credited.

note: A mutation suite that merely expects runtime output differences does not test universal-coverage integrity (SPEC 18). M4 and M6 target claim integrity directly.
